chunks: And from him, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), that he used to say:

"When a man enters the mosque and his family has already prayed, he should not call the adhan, nor call the iqamah, nor pray a voluntary prayer, until he begins with the obligatory prayer. And he should not leave it for another [mosque] until he prays in it."

key_terms.إِذَا دَخَلَ الرَّجُلُ الْمَسْجِدَ: When a man enters the mosque

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on adhan, iqamah, and voluntary prayers when entering a mosque where family has already prayed?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the protocol for a worshipper entering a mosque after the congregation has already prayed, emphasizing the preservation of the mosque's sanctity by avoiding redundant adhan and iqamah. It further instructs that one should not perform voluntary prayers in that specific mosque until the obligatory prayer is completed, thereby prioritizing the fard and maintaining the continuity of the congregational atmosphere.
